who: Charles W. Connell, medieval historian at West Virginia University, later Northern Arizona University; PhD Rutgers.

evidence.says: His CV lists a Rutgers PhD, West Virginia history teaching from 1967 to 1982 and associate-dean appointments through 1986; publications include Literary and Historical Perspectives of the Middle Ages.
The authority identifies Charles W. Connell through Literary and Historical Perspectives of the Middle Ages (1982), whose contributor note gives West Virginia University.

notes: Institution, doctorate institution, medieval field and shared publication identify the candidate. The CV does not establish residence at WVU in 1989; dissertation completion can follow departure.

who: Charles Curtis Cumberland, historian of Mexico at Michigan State University; PhD University of Texas, 1949.

who: Leroy Davis Jr., historian of African American history at Emory University; PhD Kent State University.

evidence.says: The CV records Emory history/African American Studies appointments from 1991 onward, a Kent State doctorate, and coauthorship of The African Experience in Community Development.
Emory identifies Leroy Davis as an emeritus history professor, Kent State PhD, and coauthor of African Experience in Community Development.
The Leroy Davis authority is based on The African Experience in Community Development (1980-81), reported by Kent State.

notes: The shared work, Kent State connection and Emory career identify this candidate. Doctoral year remains inconsistent: AHA gives 1989, the CV 1991, and Emory biography sections 1990 and 1988.

who: Sundiata A. Djata, historian of Africa and African American history at Northern Illinois University; PhD University of Illinois.

evidence.says: NIU lists Djata as a history professor with an Illinois PhD, author of The Bamana Empire by the Niger and Blacks at the Net.
The Illinois higher-education directory lists Robert Hanserd at Northern Illinois with Sundiata Djata and Aaron Fogelman as mentors/advisors.
The Sundiata A. Djata authority cites The Bamana Empire by the Niger (1996) and Blacks at the Net.

notes: Shared publications, university, doctoral institution and the named student/advisor connection establish the match.

who: James Donohoe, University of Arizona history professor; the AHA record gives a Harvard history PhD, 1956.

evidence.says: The indexed caption in the University of Arizona yearbook Desert (1971) identifies Dr. James Donohoe as a professor of history.
The candidate James Hugh Donohoe is identified from The Bibliography of the Convict Transports (1988), with qualifications BA and Dip. FHS.

The society profile identifies James Hugh Donohoe as a University of New England graduate in history and economic history, with a Society of Australian Genealogists diploma; it lists his works on Norfolk Island and early Australian families.

notes: The sole candidate is the Australian genealogical author James Hugh Donohoe, a different person from the Arizona faculty supervisor. Yearbook evidence was available as an indexed caption; the full page returned an access error.

who: Harold Bond Fields, Michigan State history professor, 1929-1967; University of Chicago PhD, 1942.

evidence.says: MSU Archives identifies Harold Bond Fields as a Chicago PhD in 1942 who taught history at Michigan State from 1929 until retirement in 1967.
This Harold Fields authority identifies songwriter Harold Cornelius Fields, credited on Tulips and Heather and other songs.
This Harold Fields authority identifies the author of The Refugee in the United States (1938), an NYU MA and executive director of the National League for American Citizenship.

notes: Neither supplied candidate is the Michigan State historian Harold Bond Fields.

who: Vernard Foley, historian of science and European intellectual history at Purdue University; PhD University of California, Berkeley.

evidence.says: Purdue identifies Vernard Foley as a history professor and a coauthor of the 1996 nomination letter honoring David Cassidy, whose 1976 dissertation concerned Werner Heisenberg.
Berkeley lists Vernard Foley among former graduate students in its Office for the History of Science and Technology.
The candidate authority identifies Vernard Foley as author of The Social Physics of Adam Smith (1976).
The scholarly review identifies The Social Physics of Adam Smith as a 1976 book by Vernard Foley, published by Purdue University Press.

notes: The distinctive name, Berkeley training, Purdue history appointment and history-of-science work agree. The exact 1970 doctorate year was not independently established.
